candidates.title: Manual's run loops (and recipes run-config*.lua, load-cat-foo-bar.lua, run-calculator*.lua) spin forever at BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW, which the same section calls a fixed point
candidates.component: Manual examples doc/README.md 'Loading and running machines', 'Instantiation from persistent state', 'Limiting execution', 'Progress feedback', 'Cartesi Machine templates' and their recipe copies in doc/recipes
candidates.role: Support (documentation examples and demo recipes; no deployment runs them)
candidates.location: doc/README.md ~4018-4021, 4116-4119, 4166-4172, 4248-4265, 4350-4353; doc/recipes/run-config.lua:9-11, run-config-in-chunks.lua:20, run-config-in-chunks-with-progress.lua:33, load-cat-foo-bar.lua:10, run-calculator.lua:16, run-calculator-with-new-drives.lua:25, slice-calculator-output.lua:22, run-config-with-hashes.lua:20
candidates.description: The manual says (line ~4041) 'BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW likewise signals a fixed point when mcycle reaches imcyclemax', but every example loop it prints ends only on BREAK_REASON_HALTED or BREAK_REASON_YIELDED_MANUALLY, and 'Limiting execution' says 'Any other reason ... just continues the loop'. machine::run returns get_state_break_reason(), which reports mcycle_overflow immediately on every call once mcycle >= imcyclemax, so the loops busy-spin forever without the machine changing.
candidates.trigger: Running any of these scripts on a machine (from a configuration or a stored directory, e.g. a template after a delivery set imcyclemax = mcycle + 2^48 - 1) whose guest does not yield or halt before imcyclemax.
candidates.reachability: imcyclemax is set by every state-changing delivery; a guest that spins past its per-input budget reaches the overflow fixed point. For a configuration, setting processor.registers.imcyclemax reproduces it directly.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: the hanging code is a documentation example/demo recipe, not the emulator; the threat model excludes nothing that this needs, but section 8 lists 'An application ... that never yields, and what the application loses by it' only for applications. 2 Role: support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes, the cartesi-machine CLI, and the Lua helper libraries ... Support'); these scripts are not on the honest operator's path. 3 High/Medium: a support defect is Medium only 'when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'; these scripts stand in for no operator or claim builder. 4 Critical: no. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule or obligation of this model' (manual self-contradiction in examples).
candidates.threat_to_goal: None directly; an integrator copying the documented loop into a node would hang at the overflow fixed point instead of treating it as a fixed point (R5). The manual contradicts itself on how to detect fixed points.
candidates.evidence: Created a config with processor.registers.imcyclemax = 30 over the harness accept.bin guest (cfgovf.lua in the scratch dir) and ran doc/recipes/run-config.lua on it: no termination, killed by timeout 10 s (exit 124). diff.lua showed native run, uarch run+reset and collect_mcycle_root_hashes all stop at mcycle 30 with break reason 8 (mcycle_overflow), as specified.
candidates.test_idea: Run doc/recipes/run-config.lua (or the manual's loop) under a timeout on a config with imcyclemax below the guest's yield point; require it to terminate (loop condition including BREAK_REASON_MCYCLE_OVERFLOW). Exit 1 on timeout.

candidates.title: get_initial_config() of a loaded machine (and the stored config.json) reports creation-time register values, not the values at store time as the manual promises
candidates.component: Machine API: machine::store / machine_config::store / machine::get_initial_config (C, Lua, JSON-RPC)
candidates.role: Honest operator only if a node reads registers from the initial config; otherwise support/diagnostic. When unsure: both.
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::store (m_c.store(dir), line ~520) and machine::get_initial_config (~404); src/machine-config.cpp machine_config::store; doc/README.md ~4130-4140
candidates.description: The manual says of a machine loaded from a directory: 'the values of all registers will reflect the values as they were when stored.' machine::store writes m_c (the creation config) to config.json without refreshing processor.registers / uarch.processor.registers from the shadow state, and get_initial_config returns that. The actual registers come from the stored shadow-state file, so the config's register fields are silently stale. Only iunrep is cross-checked (validate_processor_shadow). Every other register field (mcycle, pc, imcyclemax, iflags, htif.*) in get_initial_config is the value from the first creation.
candidates.trigger: Any caller that creates a machine, runs it, stores it, loads it and reads get_initial_config().processor.registers (e.g. src/cartesi-machine.lua reads initial_config.processor.registers.htif for check_cmio_htif_config and iunrep).
candidates.reachability: Every stored machine that ran at least one cycle. The guest cannot change htif ihalt/iconsole/iyield or iunrep, so the CLI checks that read them remain correct unless write_reg changed them; registers the guest changes (mcycle, pc, x*, imcyclemax after delivery) are stale.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion applies unless a deliberate write_reg is needed (only for htif fields). 2 Role: rest of the machine API; get_initial_config is not used by the emulator for transitions (only iunrep, which is validated), so no honest-operator path found that reads stale registers; CLI uses are support. 3 High/Medium: Medium 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)' could be argued since config.json is part of the stored directory and contradicts the stored shadow; but the config's registers are ignored on load, so contents and hashes are unaffected. 4 Critical: no rule broken at a reachable state (R2 'one source of truth': the stale copy is never read for a transition). 5 Low: manual contradiction on a non-security point. If a reader finds a node that takes imcyclemax/iflags from get_initial_config, the Medium reading applies.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium under the R9 'stored directory inconsistent' reading)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Indirect: a tool that trusts get_initial_config for current register values (as the manual invites) would act on wrong mcycle/imcyclemax/iflags, e.g. misjudge whether a loaded template waits at an accepted manual yield.
candidates.evidence: t1.lua: created machine from harness baremetal-minimal config, run(1000) (mcycle 1000, pc 0x80000020), store('st1'), load: get_initial_config().processor.registers.mcycle = 0 and pc = 0x80000000 while read_reg gives 1000 and 0x80000020. Also confirmed store into an existing directory fails ('File exists') as documented.
candidates.test_idea: Create, run N cycles, store, load; assert get_initial_config().processor.registers.mcycle == read_reg('mcycle') and .pc == read_reg('pc') (and likewise imcyclemax after a delivery). Exit 1 if they differ.

candidates.title: Automatic placement of flash drives/NVRAMs ignores explicitly placed ranges, so an omitted start collides instead of being 'placed to respect the alignment and overlap restrictions'
candidates.role: Rest of the machine API (configuration); creation-time, operator-controlled
candidates.description: The manual: 'If start is omitted, it is automatically placed to respect the alignment and overlap restrictions. The first flash drive is placed past RAM, then each remaining flash drive is placed past the previous. The first NVRAM is placed past the last flash drive'. adjust_starts advances its cursor only over ranges whose start was omitted; an explicitly placed drive does not move it. A drive with an explicit start at the auto cursor followed by a drive without start gets the same start, and creation fails with an overlap error; likewise the first NVRAM is placed past the last auto-placed flash drive, not past the last flash drive.
candidates.trigger: Operator configuration mixing explicit and omitted starts, e.g. flash_drive = {{start=0x80100000,length=0x1000},{length=0x1000}} with 1 MiB RAM.
candidates.reachability: Configuration-time only; fails loudly (machine not created).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: no exclusion; but the effect is a refused creation by the trusted caller. 2 Role: machine creation (honest operator in the broad sense) but no hash or proof affected. 3 High/Medium: none of the cases (no wrong hash, no damage). 4 Critical: R4 requires that accepted configurations work and that bad ones be 'rejected when the machine is created'; this rejects a valid layout the manual says is handled, it does not accept a broken one. 5 Low: 'a real defect that violates no rule', manual contradiction on placement.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None; usability/manual contradiction. No accepted configuration yields a wrong state (hash tree check_address_ranges independently enforces po2 alignment and rounded-overlap, verified).
candidates.evidence: t5.lua: 'auto after explicit' config refused with 'address range of flash drive 1 overlaps with address range of existing flash drive 0'. Other promises checked in t5.lua held: invalid hash_function, float/string registers and wrong marchid rejected; marchid -1 accepted; unaligned start and rounded-up overlap rejected by hash_tree::check_address_ranges; RAM length not page multiple rejected; HTIF getchar in a reproducible machine rejected.
candidates.test_idea: Create with flash_drive {{start=AR_RAM_START+bit_ceil(ram.length), length=4096},{length=4096}}; require success with drive 1 at a non-overlapping, aligned start. Exit 1 on the overlap error.

not_covered: Second half of the Lua interface (State hashes onward, ~4383+): proofs, verification, uarch, cmio, runtime config APIs.
JSON-RPC equivalents of create/load/store/replace_memory_range and their default sharing modes (only Lua defaults checked: create/store default SHARING_ALL, load default SHARING_NONE).

Processor backing_store.data_filename supplying a crafted shadow state (TLB slots, padding) at creation: only confirmed every TLB path calls shadow_tlb_verify_slot; no differential run with crafted TLB contents.
Register-value legality (WARL) of config registers: write_reg stores raw values; R4 excludes configs with values the spec does not allow, so not pursued.

Differential tests of unusual configs covered only bare-metal accept.bin for 30-40 mcycles (imcyclemax below mcycle, imcyclemax mid-boot, iflags X/Y/H combinations, icycleinstret, pending timer/software interrupts, mtimecmp=0): native run, uarch run+reset and collect_mcycle_root_hashes agreed. No EVM verification of those states, no Linux guest.
phtc_size=1 checked on emit-output guest (delivery, collect, 3000 logged+verified uarch steps, verify_hash_tree): correct; larger guests not tried.
dht/dpt reuse with truncate=true on a resized file (stale dirty flags for newly padded pages): reasoned only, operator-controlled.

replace_memory_range honoring create/truncate (it bypasses prepare_ar_backing_store, so create/truncate in a replacement are not applied; fails loudly) and replacement of internal ranges by internal labels (.ram, .dtb, .cmio-*, .uarch-ram), deliberate API changes; not reported.
Manual statement that image size 'must exactly match' the range length: implementation accepts shorter non-shared images (zero gap) and longer ones are refused; judged harmless, not reported.
CLI --store-config/--load-config round trip checked once (root hash equal) for a Linux config with an extra flash drive and an NVRAM; JSON format and stored-machine configs not checked.
DTB generation contents (aliases, cartesi-machine node, bootargs semantics) beyond reading dtb.cpp bounds checks.
